upstream_evidence.observed: Exact-version cProfile implementation registers sys.monitoring events and has one currentProfilerContext in its profiler object. Together with observed foreign frames, this invalidates thread-only attribution.
Upstream CPython issue documents Python 3.12 profiler tool sharing across threads; issue discussion is distinguished from version-tagged source.
Legacy profile hook is documented as thread-specific; it supplies Python call/return events. Wall timing still includes descheduling, so an independent thread CPU clock is retained.

interpretation: Eight privacy/clock/thread-isolation/exception-restoration regressions pass; the corrected installed diagnostic passes all thirteen original gates.
Every sixteenth context compile is sampled with a thread-specific legacy hook. Nineteen samples finish with no foreign events or clock errors.

The context worker records 0.346190959 total CPU seconds across 7.932015583 elapsed seconds and 317 successful compiles. Profiling overhead is included; sampled times must not be extrapolated as uninstrumented latency.

Each sampled compile projects the isolated environment once. The nine importlib metadata search-root probes arise from one force-only compatibility-distribution discovery; production auto mode does not use that search.

Current environment projection iterates items, reading every value before filtering. A key-first projection can preserve admitted output while avoiding rejected-value reads; this remains a proposed source correction here.
Binary/manifest/path invalidation, approval authority, runtime Python gate and every measurement limit remain unchanged. No product efficiency benefit is claimed.
